items.t: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis (PJP): treatment and prevention. Toxoplasmosis: treatment and prophylaxis. Nocardiosis: treatment.

src.q: Treatment and prevention of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis or "PJP". Treatment and prophylaxis of toxoplasmosis. Treatment of nocardiosis.

items.t: Acute uncomplicated UTI, acute otitis media and acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis ONLY when there is bacterial evidence of sensitivity and good reason to prefer the combination over a single antibiotic.

src.q: The following infections may be treated with Co-Trimoxazole where there is bacterial evidence of sensitivity to Co-Trimoxazole and good reason to prefer the combination of antibiotics in Co-Trimoxazole to a single antibiotic
Acute uncomplicated urinary tract infection. Acute otitis media. Acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis.

items.t: UK licence limits UTI, otitis media and bronchitis use to proven sensitivity plus good reason to prefer the combination. Use only where benefits outweigh risks; consider a single effective antibacterial.

src.q: The combination of antibiotics in Co-Trimoxazole should only be used where, in the judgement of the physician, the benefits of treatment outweigh any possible risks; consideration should be given to the use of a single effective antibacterial agent.

items.t: Do not use for streptococcal pharyngitis due to Group A beta-haemolytic streptococci.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should not be used in the treatment of streptococcal pharyngitis due to Group A beta-haemolytic streptococci

items.t: Tablets and the adult suspension are licensed for adults and children over 12; the paediatric suspension for children 12 years and under (6 weeks or older).

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole tablets are indicated in adults and children over 12 years
Co-Trimoxazole Paediatric Suspension is indicated in children aged 12 years and under (≥6 weeks)

items.t: Adults and children over 12: 2 tablets (480 mg) every 12 hours = 1 Forte tablet (960 mg) every 12 hours = 10 ml adult suspension every 12 hours. Continue until symptom-free for 2 days (most need at least 5 days); reassess if no improvement after 7 days.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years : STANDARD DOSAGE: 2 tablets every 12 hours
Adults and children over 12 years: STANDARD DOSAGE: 1 tablet every 12 hours
>18 years old 10 ml every 12 hours

Treatment should be continued until the patient has been symptom free for two days; the majority will require treatment for at least 5 days. If clinical improvement is not evident after 7 days therapy, the patient should be reassessed.

items.t: Acute uncomplicated lower UTI: short-term therapy of 1 to 3 days is an alternative to the standard course.

src.q: As an alternative to Standard Dosage for acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infections, short-term therapy of 1 to 3 days duration has been shown to be effective.

items.t: PJP treatment (adults and children over 12): trimethoprim 20 mg/kg + sulfamethoxazole 100 mg/kg per day in two or more divided doses for 2 weeks.

src.q: A higher dosage is recommended, using 20 mg trimethoprim and 100 mg sulfamethoxazole per kg of body weight per day in two or more divided doses for two weeks.

items.t: PJP prevention (adults and children over 12), choose one: 160 mg/800 mg DAILY 7 days a week; OR 160 mg/800 mg three times a WEEK on alternate days; OR 320 mg/1600 mg per day in two divided doses three times a WEEK on alternate days. Total daily dose must not exceed 320 mg trimethoprim / 1600 mg sulfamethoxazole.

src.q: 160 mg trimethoprim/800 mg sulfamethoxazole daily 7 days per week. 160 mg trimethoprim/800 mg sulfamethoxazole three times per week on alternate days. 320 mg trimethoprim/1600 mg sulfamethoxazole per day in two divided doses three times per week on alternate days.
The total daily dose should not exceed 320 mg trimethoprim and 1600 mg sulfamethoxazole.

items.t: Nocardiosis (adults over 18): no consensus; 6 to 8 tablets (480 mg) daily for up to 3 months have been used. Toxoplasmosis: no consensus; PJP prevention doses may suit prophylaxis.

src.q: Adult doses of 6 to 8 tablets daily for up to 3 months have been used.
For prophylaxis, however, the dosages suggested for prevention of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonitis may be appropriate.

items.t: Elderly: standard dose unless otherwise specified; take particular care (more susceptible to serious adverse effects).

src.q: Unless otherwise specified standard dosage applies.
Particular care is always advisable when treating elderly patients

items.t: Must not be given in the first 6 weeks of life (listed in SmPC 4.3 of all four co-trimoxazole SmPCs). Separately, the breastfeeding paragraph of 4.6 says co-trimoxazole should be avoided in infants younger than 8 weeks (predisposition to hyperbilirubinaemia). It sits in the breastfeeding text, so this tool applies it to breastfeeding; the paediatric suspension is still licensed from 6 weeks.

src.q: Co-trimoxazole should not be given to infants during the first 6 weeks of life.
Co-Trimoxazole Paediatric Suspension is indicated in children aged 12 years and under (≥6 weeks)
Additionally, administration of Co-Trimoxazole should be avoided in infants younger than eight weeks in view of the predisposition of young infants to hyperbilirubinaemia.

items.t: Children 12 years and under (paediatric suspension): about trimethoprim 6 mg/kg + sulfamethoxazole 30 mg/kg per day in two equal doses. By age: 6-12 years 10 ml every 12 hours; 6 months-5 years 5 ml every 12 hours; 6 weeks-5 months 2.5 ml every 12 hours.

src.q: The standard dosage for children is equivalent to approximately 6 mg trimethoprim and 30 mg sulfamethoxazole per kg body weight per day, given in two equally divided doses.
6 to 12 years 10 ml every 12 hours 6 months to 5 years 5 ml every 12 hours 6 weeks to 5 months 2.5 ml every 12 hours

items.t: PJP treatment, children 12 and under: trimethoprim 20 mg/kg + sulfamethoxazole 100 mg/kg per day in two or more divided doses for 2 weeks.

src.q: Treatment - Children aged 12 years and under: A higher dosage is recommended, using 20 mg trimethoprim and 100 mg sulfamethoxazole per kg of body weight per day in two or more divided doses for two weeks.

items.t: PJP prevention, children 12 and under: about 6 mg/kg trimethoprim per day, as the age-banded volume every 12 hours either 7 days a WEEK or 3 days a WEEK (alternate or consecutive days), or as double the volume ONCE a day on 3 consecutive days a WEEK (e.g. 6-12 years: 10 ml every 12 hours, or 20 ml once a day). Total daily dose must not exceed 320 mg trimethoprim / 1600 mg sulfamethoxazole.

src.q: 6 to 12 years 10 ml every 12 hours, seven days per week
6 to 12 years 20 ml once a day, three times per week on consecutive days
The total daily dose should not exceed 320 mg trimethoprim and 1600 mg sulfamethoxazole.

items.t: Children over 12 to under 18 (adult suspension): 10 ml every 12 hours.

src.q: >12 to <18 years old 10 ml every 12 hours

items.t: No information on renal failure dosing in children aged 12 and under.

src.q: No information is available for children aged 12 years and under with renal failure.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance(s) sulphonamides, trimethoprim, co-trimoxazole or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Severe liver impairment (Forte tablet and adult suspension SmPCs: contra-indicated; 480 mg tablet SmPC: should not be given; all in section 4.3).

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should not be given to patients with severe impairment of liver function.
Contra-indicated in patients with severe impairment of liver function.

items.t: Severe renal insufficiency where repeated plasma concentration measurements cannot be done.

src.q: Contra-indicated in severe renal insufficiency where repeated measurements of the plasma concentration cannot be performed.

items.t: Infants in the first 6 weeks of life.

src.q: Co-trimoxazole should not be given to infants during the first 6 weeks of life.

items.t: History of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with trimethoprim and/or sulfonamides.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should not be given to patients with a history of drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia with use of trimethoprim and/or sulphonamides.

items.t: Acute porphyria.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should not be given to patients with acute porphyria.

items.t: First trimester of pregnancy.

src.q: First trimester of pregnancy (see section 4.6).

items.t: Fatal reactions (very rare): SJS, TEN, fulminant hepatic necrosis, agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, other blood dyscrasias, respiratory hypersensitivity.

src.q: Fatalities, although very rare, have occurred due to severe reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis, fulminant hepatic necrosis, agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, other blood dyscrasias and hypersensitivity of the respiratory tract.

items.t: SJS/TEN/DRESS: highest risk in the first weeks; stop if signs appear and never restart. AGEP at start of treatment: stop and do not re-administer.

src.q: The highest risk for occurrence of SJS or TEN is within the first weeks of treatment.
If the patient has developed SJS, TEN and DRESS with the use of Co-Trimoxazole, the treatment must not be re-started in this patient at any time.

items.t: G6PD deficiency: haemolysis may occur.

src.q: In glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G-6-PD) deficient patients haemolysis may occur.

items.t: Folate: monthly blood counts advisable for long courses, folate-deficient patients or the elderly. Folinic acid may be considered but can reduce antimicrobial efficacy.

src.q: Regular monthly blood counts are advisable when Co-Trimoxazole is given for long periods, or to folate deficient patients or to the elderly
Supplementation with folinic acid may be considered during treatment but this should be initiated with caution due to possible interference with antimicrobial efficacy

items.t: Serious haematological disorders: do not give except under careful supervision.

src.q: Except under careful supervision Co-Trimoxazole should not be given to patients with serious haematological disorders

items.t: Hyperkalaemia and hyponatraemia: close potassium monitoring in at-risk patients. Metabolic acidosis reported.

src.q: Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted in patients at risk of hyperkalaemia and hyponatraemia.
Co-Trimoxazole has been associated with metabolic acidosis

items.t: Severe atopy or bronchial asthma: give with caution.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should be given with caution to patients with severe atopy or bronchial asthma.

items.t: Porphyria (known or suspected risk): avoid.

src.q: The administration of Co-Trimoxazole to patients known or suspected to be at risk of porphyria should be avoided.

items.t: Keep adequate urine output (crystalluria risk, higher in malnutrition).

src.q: An adequate urinary output should be maintained at all times.

items.t: Respiratory toxicity (possible ARDS) and haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH): stop if these develop.

src.q: In such circumstances, co-trimoxazole should be discontinued and appropriate treatment given.
If diagnosis of HLH is established, co-trimoxazole treatment should be discontinued.

items.t: Methotrexate: co-trimoxazole may raise free methotrexate levels; the co-trimoxazole SmPC says consider a folate supplement. SPS: avoid the combination (risk of severe bone marrow suppression, possibly delayed). One methotrexate tablet SmPC lists this combination under 4.3 Contraindications (should not be used concomitantly).

src.q: Methotrexate: co-trimoxazole may increase the free plasma levels of methotrexate.
Avoid prescribing co-trimoxazole or trimethoprim with methotrexate, due to the risk of severe bone marrow suppression.
Methotrexate tablets should not be used concomitantly with drugs with antifolate properties (e.g. co-trimoxazole)

items.t: Warfarin: anticoagulant effect potentiated; careful control of anticoagulation advised.

src.q: Careful control of the anticoagulant therapy during treatment with Co-Trimoxazole is advisable.

items.t: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone): caution, clinically relevant hyperkalaemia possible.

src.q: Hyperkalaemia: caution should be exercised in patients taking any other drugs that can cause hyperkalaemia, for example ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and potassium-sparing diuretics such as spironolactone.

items.t: Thiazide diuretics in elderly: increased thrombocytopenia risk.

src.q: Diuretics (thiazides): in elderly patients concurrently receiving diuretics, mainly thiazides, there appears to be an increased risk of thrombocytopenia with or without purpura.

items.t: Others not in master list: phenytoin (monitor levels), digoxin (raised levels in elderly), ciclosporin (renal deterioration), zidovudine, pyrimethamine, repaglinide (hypoglycaemia), sulfonylureas, lamivudine, azathioprine, oral contraceptives (antibiotic advice).

src.q: Close monitoring of the patient's condition and serum phenytoin levels are advisable.
Repaglinide: trimethoprim may increase the exposure of repaglinide which may result in hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Lab tests: trimethoprim may cause ~10% overestimation of serum creatinine (alkaline picrate method) and interferes with some methotrexate assays.

src.q: This may result in overestimation of serum/plasma creatinine of the order of 10%.

items.t: Adults and children over 12, by creatinine clearance (CrCl): over 30 ml/min standard dose; 15 to 30 ml/min half dose (480 mg tablets: 1 tablet every 12 hours; Forte 960 mg tablets: 1 tablet per DAY; adult suspension: 5 ml every 12 hours); under 15 ml/min not recommended. No information for children 12 and under with renal failure.

src.q: Creatinine Clearance (ml/min) Recommended Dosage >30 2 tablets every 12 hours 15 to 30 1 tablet every 12 hours <15 Not recommended
> 30 1 tablet every 12 hours 15 to 30 1 tablet per day <15 Not recommended
Creatinine Clearance (ml/min) Recommended Dosage >30 10 ml every 12 hours 15 to 30 5 ml every 12 hours <15 Not recommended
No information is available for children aged 12 years and under with renal failure.

items.t: Measure plasma sulfamethoxazole every 2 to 3 days (12 hours post-dose); interrupt if total sulfamethoxazole exceeds 150 microgram/ml until below 120 microgram/ml.

src.q: If the concentration of total sulfamethoxazole exceeds 150 microgram/ml then treatment should be interrupted until the value falls below 120 microgram/ml.

items.t: Contraindicated in severe renal insufficiency where repeated plasma measurements cannot be done.

src.q: Contra-indicated in severe renal insufficiency where repeated measurements of the plasma concentration cannot be performed.

items.t: Severe liver impairment: should not be given. No dosing data for hepatic impairment.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole should not be given to patients with severe impairment of liver function.
Impaired hepatic function: No data are available relating to dosage in patients with impaired hepatic function.

items.t: First trimester: contraindicated (trimethoprim; miscarriage and malformations including neural tube defects, oral clefts, heart defects).

src.q: Trimethoprim is contraindicated during the first trimester of pregnancy (see section 4.3).

items.t: Second and third trimesters: avoid unless clinically necessary. Consider folate supplementation if used.

src.q: In the second and third trimesters, use should be avoided, unless clinically necessary.
Folate supplementation should be considered if Co-Trimoxazole is used in pregnancy.

items.t: Near delivery: risk of neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia and theoretical kernicterus. Avoid in late pregnancy where mother or infant has or is at particular risk of hyperbilirubinaemia.

src.q: there may be a risk of precipitating or exacerbating neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia, with an associated theoretical risk of kernicterus, when Co-Trimoxazole is administered to the mother near the time of delivery.
Administration of Co-Trimoxazole should be avoided in late pregnancy and in lactating mothers where the mother or infant has, or is at particular risk of developing, hyperbilirubinaemia.

items.t: Both components pass into breast milk. Avoid where mother or infant has, or is at particular risk of, hyperbilirubinaemia. SmPC also says avoid in infants younger than 8 weeks (young infants prone to hyperbilirubinaemia).

src.q: The components of Co-Trimoxazole (trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole) are excreted in breast milk.
administration of Co-Trimoxazole should be avoided in infants younger than eight weeks in view of the predisposition of young infants to hyperbilirubinaemia.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception requirement in the co-trimoxazole SmPCs (4.5 only notes antibiotic/oral contraceptive advice). No BUMPS co-trimoxazole leaflet found (URL variants returned 404).

items.t: Very common: hyperkalaemia. Common: headache, nausea, diarrhoea, rash, fungal overgrowth.

src.q: Very common Hyperkalaemia.
Common Nausea, diarrhoea.
Common Overgrowth fungal.

items.t: SJS/TEN/DRESS/AGEP: stop immediately; never restart after SJS/TEN/DRESS.

src.q: Co-Trimoxazole treatment should be discontinued (see section 4.8) and an alternative treatment considered (as appropriate).

items.t: Blood dyscrasias (agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, megaloblastic anaemia, thrombocytopenia), haemolysis in G6PD deficiency.

src.q: Very rare Leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, anaemia megaloblastic, aplastic anaemia

items.t: Respiratory hypersensitivity (cough, dyspnoea, lung infiltrates) can be fatal; hepatic necrosis; aseptic meningitis; circulatory shock (mainly immunocompromised).

src.q: Cough, dyspnoea and lung infiltration may be early indicators of respiratory hypersensitivity which, while very rare, has been fatal
Jaundice cholestatic and hepatic necrosis may be fatal.

items.t: High PJP doses: severe hypersensitivity reactions may require stopping; rhabdomyolysis reported in HIV patients.

src.q: At the high dosages used for PJP management severe hypersensitivity reactions have been reported, necessitating cessation of therapy.

items.t: Long courses, folate-deficient or elderly patients: monthly blood counts.

src.q: Regular monthly blood counts are advisable when Co-Trimoxazole is given for long periods, or to folate deficient patients or to the elderly

items.t: Potassium in patients at risk of hyperkalaemia/hyponatraemia.

src.q: Close monitoring of serum potassium is warranted in patients at risk of hyperkalaemia and hyponatraemia.

items.t: Renal impairment: plasma sulfamethoxazole every 2-3 days; interrupt above 150 microgram/ml.

src.q: Measurements of plasma concentration of sulfamethoxazole at intervals of 2 to 3 days are recommended in samples obtained 12 hours after administration of Co-Trimoxazole.

items.t: Stop for skin reactions suggesting SJS/TEN/DRESS/AGEP, HLH, or pulmonary signs suggesting ARDS.

src.q: If symptoms or signs of SJS, TEN (e.g. progressive skin rash often with blisters or mucosal lesions) or DRESS (e.g. fever, eosinophilia) are present

items.t: Oral. May be better taken with some food or drink to reduce GI upset.

src.q: It may be preferable to take Co-Trimoxazole with some food or drink to minimise the possibility of gastrointestinal disturbances.

items.t: Drink enough fluid to keep a good urine output.

src.q: An adequate urinary output should be maintained at all times.

items.t: Report any rash, blisters, mouth sores or fever at once, especially in the first weeks.

src.q: Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.

items.t: Women using oral contraceptives: SmPC advises temporarily adding a barrier method while on antibiotics.

src.q: Women on treatment with antibiotics should temporarily use a barrier method in addition to the oral contraceptive, or choose another method of contraception.
